questions.q: What does a Subledger Accounting Method specify for each subledger application a company uses?
options: A list of every possible AAD that could ever be used
Exactly one AAD to use for that application
A single account rule, with no AAD involved at all
The ledger's functional currency
questions.explain: For every subledger application in use, the accounting method specifies exactly one AAD that will govern accounting for that application.

questions.q: Can a single accounting method reference a seeded AAD for one application and a custom AAD for another application?
options: No, a method must be entirely seeded or entirely custom
Yes — each subledger application's AAD assignment within the method is independent of every other application's assignment
Only if both applications are Payables
No, custom AADs can never be referenced by any method
questions.explain: It is common and normal for a method to mix seeded and custom AADs, since each application's assignment is independent.

questions.q: What happens if a subledger application in use has no AAD assigned within the active accounting method?
options: The application automatically uses the Payables AAD instead
Nothing changes; AAD assignment has no real effect
Accounting events raised by that application for that ledger cannot be processed, because there is nowhere to look up rules
The General Ledger posts a default journal entry automatically
questions.explain: Without an AAD mapped for an application, Create Accounting has no rules to apply, and that application's events cannot be accounted.

questions.q: Why is a missing AAD assignment described as a common troubleshooting root cause?
options: Because it is the first thing listed in this lesson, with no further relevance
Because it directly explains a very common real-world symptom: a transaction that never generates a journal entry
Because it only affects test environments, never production
Because missing AAD assignments are impossible to diagnose
questions.explain: A missing AAD assignment for a given application is a frequent cause of transactions that silently fail to generate accounting, which is covered further in the troubleshooting lesson.

questions.q: How does an accounting method relate to the configuration chain covered across this chapter?
options: It is unrelated to AADs and rule sets entirely
It is the final assembly step: individual rules became rule sets, rule sets became AADs, and AADs for every application are assembled into one method
It comes before journal line rules are even created
It replaces the need for a Chart of Accounts
questions.explain: The accounting method sits at the top of the configuration chain, assembling one AAD per subledger application into a single usable configuration.
